description_good_justification: The README opens with what the extension is: a pair of accessible, high-contrast VS Code colour themes, dark and light, tuned for WCAG AA contrast: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/README.md
interact_justification: The README explains how to install the extension from the Marketplace, use it, give feedback (GitHub issues) and contribute: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/README.md#installation
contribution_justification: The contribution process (issues, pull requests, checks, sign-off): https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-code
contribution_requirements_justification: Contribution requirements, including coding style, the contrast tests and how to add a colour, are in CONTRIBUTING.md: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-code
documentation_basics_justification: Installation from the Marketplace, how to select the themes, and the palette: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/README.md#installation
documentation_interface_justification: The extension has no API; its external interface is the two themes, named "Accessible (AA) Dark" and "Accessible (AA) Light", which users pick in Preferences: Color Theme. The README documents both and their palettes: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/README.md#usage
sites_https_justification: The repository and the Marketplace listing are served over HTTPS: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme
discussion_justification: GitHub issues and pull requests are searchable, addressable by URL and open to anyone with a GitHub account: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/issues
english_justification: All documentation is in English, and reports and comments in English are accepted.
maintained_justification: The project is actively maintained, with releases and changes in November 2026: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/releases
repo_track_justification: Git records who changed what and when: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/commits/main
repo_interim_justification: Every change is a public commit and pull request between releases, not only the releases themselves.
version_unique_justification: Every release has a unique version, tagged as <version>: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/tags
version_semver_justification: Semantic Versioning, with versions picked from conventional commits; renaming or removing a theme or narrowing engines.vscode is a breaking change: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#commits-and-pull-requests
version_tags_justification: Each release is tagged in git: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/tags
release_notes_justification: A CHANGELOG.md generated from conventional commits, also published as GitHub release notes: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No release has fixed a publicly known vulnerability in the published extension, and the repository has no security advisories. Such a fix would be listed in the release notes and a GitHub security advisory.
report_process_justification: How to report a bug, with an issue template: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#reporting-bugs
report_responses_justification: Every issue is assigned to the maintainer when it is opened. No one outside the project has filed a bug report in the last 12 months, so none is unanswered.
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests are answered in their GitHub issue. No one outside the project has filed one in the last 12 months, so none is unanswered.
report_archive_justification: All issues and pull requests stay public and searchable on GitHub: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private reports through GitHub private vulnerability reporting or by email: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: Reports are acknowledged within 7 days; no vulnerability has been reported in the last 6 months: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#how-reports-are-handled
build_justification: npm run package builds the .vsix with vsce, and npm run check:pack checks it: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#development
build_common_tools_justification: npm and vsce, the standard packaging tool for VS Code extensions.
build_floss_tools_justification: npm, Node.js and vsce (@vscode/vsce, MIT) are all FLOSS.
test_justification: A node:test suite, run with npm test, checks the WCAG contrast of every syntax and UI text colour in both themes and the README palette tables, and npm run check:pack checks the built .vsix: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
test_invocation_justification: npm test, the standard way to run tests in an npm project.
test_most_justification: Every syntax colour and every UI text colour in both theme files is checked by the contrast tests against its background, except one key listed with its reason (checkbox.foreground, whose background the themes leave unset). The test helpers are at 98.8% of lines (Node test coverage), and check:pack runs on the real package in every CI run.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: The Checks workflow lints, checks the format, tests, packs and checks the package on every pull request and every push to main: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/.github/workflows/check.yml
test_policy_justification: New or changed colours must pass the contrast tests, and bug fixes must come with a regression test: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
tests_are_added_justification: Recent changes came with tests: the light theme comment contrast fix (#67) with the syntax contrast test, the UI contrast fix (#68) with the UI contrast test, and the README palette corrections (#70) with the README palette test.
tests_documented_added_justification: The tests policy is part of the instructions for contributing code: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
warnings_justification: ESLint (eslint-config-phun-ky, with stylistic and Prettier rules) runs on the JavaScript and Markdown files, and Prettier checks the JSON and YAML files, including the themes.
warnings_fixed_justification: Lint has no errors and no warnings (eslint . --max-warnings 0), and the Prettier check passes.
warnings_strict_justification: Lint and format errors fail the Checks workflow; the scripts and tests are ES modules, which always run in strict mode.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer knows how to design secure software. The principles applied: data only, with no code in the extension, an allowlisted package checked file by file, no shipped dependencies, least-privilege CI tokens, pinned Actions, and publishing through Marketplace Trusted Publishing. What the extension guarantees and does not: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer knows the common errors for this kind of software: code smuggled into the extension (rejected by check:pack, which fails on any unexpected file), supply chain (no shipped dependencies, locked and reviewed development dependencies, pinned Actions) and stolen publishing credentials (none: Trusted Publishing from a main-only environment): https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
crypto_published_justification: The extension contains no code and does no network access: it is two JSON colour themes. See the security expectations: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
crypto_call_justification: The extension contains no code and does no network access: it is two JSON colour themes. See the security expectations: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations

crypto_keylength_justification: The extension contains no code and does no network access: it is two JSON colour themes. See the security expectations: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
crypto_working_justification: The extension contains no code and does no network access: it is two JSON colour themes. See the security expectations: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations

crypto_pfs_justification: The extension contains no code and does no network access: it is two JSON colour themes. See the security expectations: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
crypto_password_storage_justification: The extension contains no code and does no network access: it is two JSON colour themes. See the security expectations: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
crypto_random_justification: The extension contains no code and does no network access: it is two JSON colour themes. See the security expectations: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
delivery_mitm_justification: The extension is delivered by the Visual Studio Marketplace over HTTPS, signed by the Marketplace and verified by VS Code on install, and the repository by GitHub over HTTPS: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hashes are fetched over HTTP; the Marketplace and GitHub are served over HTTPS only.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: The published extension ships no dependencies and has no known vulnerabilities (npm audit --omit=dev runs before every release). Development tooling alerts are fixed or accepted as described in the security policy: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerability has been found in the published extension.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials are in the repository; GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enabled: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#secrets
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (GitHub default setup) analyses every pull request and push to main, and ESLint runs on every pull request.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL analyses the JavaScript and the GitHub Actions workflows on every push to main and every pull request, and the ruleset on main requires its results, with no errors and no high or critical security alerts, before merging: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#code-scanning
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CodeQL has no open alerts; the ruleset blocks merging with a high or critical one.
static_analysis_often_justification: On every pull request and every push to main.
dynamic_analysis_justification: The extension has no code to run, and no fuzzing or other dynamic analysis is applied to the tooling.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The extension is JSON data, and the tooling is JavaScript on Node.js, which is memory-safe; there is no C, C++ or other memory-unsafe code.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The extension has no code that could carry assertions; the checks are the contrast tests and check:pack, run before release.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis is run, so it has found nothing to fix.
achieve_passing_justification: The passing badge is in progress: https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/16534
dco_justification: Every commit must be signed off under the Developer Certificate of Origin, checked on every pull request by the DCO app and required by the ruleset on main: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#developer-certificate-of-origin
governance_justification: The maintainer-led governance model and how decisions are made: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
roles_responsibilities_justification: The maintainer and contributor roles and their responsibilities, and who holds them: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
access_continuity_justification: One maintainer holds the access to the repository and the Marketplace publisher today. Releases use Marketplace Trusted Publishing (no personal token) and the themes are MIT-licensed, but no second person holds access yet: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
bus_factor_justification: The project has one maintainer, so the bus factor is 1: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/graphs/contributors
documentation_roadmap_justification: What the project plans to do, consider and not do until November 2027, linking the issues: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/ROADMAP.md
documentation_architecture_justification: The theme files, the manifest, the package allowlist, the pack check and the tests: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#architecture
documentation_security_justification: What users can and cannot rely on: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
documentation_quick_start_justification: Install from the Extensions view and pick a theme in Preferences: Color Theme: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/README.md#installation
documentation_current_justification: npm test fails when the README palette tables differ from the theme files, and documentation defects are fixed as normal changes, as in #70.
documentation_achievements_justification: The README shows the OpenSSF Best Practices and Scorecard badges: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/README.md
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: Accessibility is what the project delivers: every syntax colour and every UI text colour the themes set reaches WCAG 2.x AA contrast (4.5:1) against its background, and npm test checks it on every pull request. The project has no website of its own; its documentation is Markdown on GitHub and the Marketplace: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/README.md#accessibility
internationalization_justification: The themes contain no text for end users, only colours.
sites_password_security_justification: The project sites (GitHub and the Marketplace) store no passwords for external users.
maintenance_or_update_justification: Only the latest release is supported, and VS Code updates extensions to it automatically; fixes are released as a new version: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerabilities have been reported to the project in the last 12 months; the repository has no security advisories.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: Reports are made privately through GitHub private vulnerability reporting or by email. Acknowledgement within 7 days, assessment, a fix in a private GitHub security advisory, coordinated disclosure and credit: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#how-reports-are-handled
coding_standards_justification: JavaScript and Markdown follow the project ESLint configuration (eslint-config-phun-ky) and Prettier, JSON and YAML follow Prettier, and contributions must pass npm run style:lint and npm run style:format-check: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#coding-style
coding_standards_enforced_justification: The Checks workflow runs ESLint (with Prettier) and the Prettier check on every pull request, and the ruleset on main requires it to pass before merging.
build_standard_variables_justification: Nothing is compiled: the .vsix is a zip of the theme files and the manifest.
build_preserve_debug_justification: Nothing is compiled, minified or stripped: the theme files ship exactly as they are in the repository.
build_non_recursive_justification: npm run package runs vsce once, which packs every file into one .vsix.
build_repeatable_justification: Rebuilding the tag 1.0.47 gives the same eight files, but not a bit-for-bit identical .vsix: the zip records file times, and the packaged CHANGELOG differs (#93). The contributed theme files are identical.
installation_common_justification: The extension is installed and removed through VS Code: the Extensions view, or code --install-extension phun-ky.vscode-accessible-theme and code --uninstall-extension phun-ky.vscode-accessible-theme.
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installation is done entirely by VS Code, which honours its standard location settings (--extensions-dir, VSCODE_EXTENSIONS). The extension has no install scripts.
installation_development_quick_justifica: git clone, npm ci and npm test give the full development and test environment, and F5 opens an Extension Development Host with the themes: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#development
external_dependencies_justification: The development dependencies are listed in package.json and locked in package-lock.json; the extension ships none: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/package.json
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot checks npm dependencies and GitHub Actions weekly, dependency review checks every pull request, and npm audit runs before every release: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
updateable_reused_components_justificati: No third-party code is copied into the repository; all external components come from npm through package.json and the lockfile, none is shipped in the extension, and Dependabot opens update pull requests.
interfaces_current_justification: The themes use the current VS Code colour theme format (colors, tokenColors, semanticTokenColors), the tooling is ES modules on Node 24, vsce 4.1 with Trusted Publishing, and current GitHub Actions pinned to commit SHAs.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: The Checks workflow lints, checks the format, runs the contrast tests, packs the extension and checks the package on every pull request and push to main, reporting results as GitHub checks.
regression_tests_added50_justification: Every bug fix in the last six months came with a test that fails without it: the light theme comment contrast (#67) with the syntax contrast test, the light theme UI contrast (#68) with the UI contrast test, and the README palette errors (#70) with the README palette test.
test_statement_coverage80_justification: The extension is data: every syntax colour and every UI text colour in both theme files is checked by the contrast tests, except one key listed with its reason. The test helpers are at 98.8% of lines and 93.6% of branches (Node test coverage), and check:pack runs on the real package in every CI run.
test_policy_mandated_justification: New or changed colours must pass the contrast tests, bug fixes must come with a regression test, and new helpers or scripts with tests: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
implement_secure_design_justification: Secure design principles applied (economy of mechanism, fail-safe defaults, least privilege, open design, minimal dependencies): https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md#secure-design-principles
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The extension contains no code and does no network access: it is two JSON colour themes. See the security expectations: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
crypto_credential_agility_justification: The extension contains no code and does no network access: it is two JSON colour themes. See the security expectations: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
crypto_used_network_justification: The extension contains no code and does no network access: it is two JSON colour themes. See the security expectations: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
crypto_tls12_justification: The extension contains no code and does no network access: it is two JSON colour themes. See the security expectations: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: The extension contains no code and does no network access: it is two JSON colour themes. See the security expectations: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: The extension contains no code and does no network access: it is two JSON colour themes. See the security expectations: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
signed_releases_justification: The project does not sign its releases itself. The Marketplace signs every version it serves and VS Code verifies that signature on install, and the GitHub release lists the SHA-256 digest of the same file, but the signing key is the Marketplace's: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases
version_tags_signed_justification: Release tags are annotated but not signed.
input_validation_justification: The extension takes no input: it has no code, commands or settings, and VS Code reads its two theme files as colour values.
hardening_justification: Data only, an allowlisted package (.vscodeignore) checked file by file before every publish, no shipped dependencies, read-only CI permissions with SHA-pinned actions, CodeQL on every change, and Trusted Publishing from a main-only environment.
assurance_case_justification: What is protected, the threat model, trust boundaries, secure design principles, the common weaknesses countered and the known gaps: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md
osps_ac_01_01_justification: The maintainer, the only person with access, uses two-factor authentication on GitHub, which GitHub requires for code contributors. Anyone given access later must use it too: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#becoming-a-maintainer
osps_ac_02_01_justification: GitHub requires a role to be chosen for every collaborator invited to the repository, and the governance requires the lowest role that fits: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#becoming-a-maintainer
osps_ac_03_01_justification: The ruleset on main requires changes to arrive through a pull request with passing checks. Only the maintainer, as administrator, can bypass it, which the release workflow uses to push its commit and tag.
osps_ac_03_02_justification: A separate ruleset on main, with no bypass, blocks deleting the branch and force pushes.
osps_br_01_01_justification: No workflow interpolates untrusted metadata, such as pull request titles or branch names, into a script; github.actor is passed through an environment variable: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish.yml
osps_br_01_03_justification: Pull requests run on the pull_request event, where forks get no secrets. The labeler runs on pull_request_target but never checks out or runs pull request code, with only pull-requests: write. Publishing runs only after a merge, in an environment only main can deploy to.
osps_br_03_01_justification: All official channels use HTTPS: the GitHub repository and the Visual Studio Marketplace: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme
osps_br_03_02_justification: The extension is distributed by the Visual Studio Marketplace over HTTPS, and the Marketplace signs every version, which VS Code verifies on install: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases
osps_br_07_01_justification: GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enabled and blocks commits that contain secrets; secrets are kept only in GitHub Actions secrets: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#secrets
osps_do_01_01_justification: Installation, how to select the themes, and the palette: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/README.md#installation

osps_le_02_02_justification: The released extension is under the MIT licence, declared in package.json: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/LICENSE

osps_le_03_02_justification: The published .vsix includes the licence text (extension/LICENSE.txt), which check:pack requires: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_qa_01_02_justification: The full git history, with authors and dates, is public: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/commits/main
osps_qa_02_01_justification: Direct dependencies are listed in package.json, with every version locked in package-lock.json: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/package.json
osps_qa_04_01_justification: The project has a single repository.
osps_qa_05_01_justification: No generated executables are committed: the .vsix is built in CI and ignored by git.
osps_qa_05_02_justification: The only binary files are four PNG images in public/ (screenshots of the themes); there are no executables or other unreviewable binaries.
osps_vm_02_01_justification: Security contacts (email and GitHub private vulnerability reporting): https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
osps_ac_04_01_justification: Every workflow sets read-only permissions at the top level, and jobs ask only for what they need: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/.github/workflows/check.yml
osps_br_02_01_justification: Every release has a unique Semantic Versioning version, tagged as <version>: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/releases
osps_br_04_01_justification: A CHANGELOG.md generated from conventional commits, listing features, fixes and breaking changes, also published as GitHub release notes: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
osps_br_05_01_justification: Dependencies are installed with npm ci from the lockfile in every pipeline: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish.yml
osps_br_06_01_justification: Releases are not signed by the project, and the GitHub release lists the file's digest without a signed manifest. The Marketplace signs the copy it serves: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases
osps_do_06_01_justification: How dependencies are chosen, obtained and tracked: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
osps_gv_01_01_justification: Who has access to the repository and the Marketplace publisher: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
osps_gv_01_02_justification: The maintainer and contributor roles and their responsibilities: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
osps_gv_03_02_justification: Requirements for contributions: style, tests, sign-off, commits and pull requests: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-code
osps_le_01_01_justification: Every commit must carry a Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off, checked on every pull request by the DCO app and required by the ruleset on main: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#developer-certificate-of-origin
osps_qa_03_01_justification: The ruleset on main requires the status checks (check, DCO and dependency-review) and CodeQL results to pass before merging; only an administrator can bypass it.
osps_qa_06_01_justification: The Checks workflow runs the tests and the pack check on every pull request, and must pass before merging: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/.github/workflows/check.yml
osps_sa_01_01_justification: The architecture (the theme files, the manifest, the package allowlist, the pack check and the tests): https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#architecture
osps_sa_02_01_justification: The extension has no API; its interface is the two themes, documented with their names and palettes in the README: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/README.md#palette
osps_sa_03_01_justification: The assurance case assesses the most likely and impactful security problems: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md
osps_vm_01_01_justification: Coordinated disclosure, with acknowledgement within 7 days and a fix within 30 days for serious issues: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#how-reports-are-handled
osps_vm_03_01_justification: Private reporting through GitHub private vulnerability reporting or the security email: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
osps_vm_04_01_justification: Vulnerabilities are published as GitHub security advisories when fixed: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/security/advisories
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Each job declares only the permissions it needs, for example the labeler has pull-requests: write and publishing has id-token: write: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/.github/workflows/label.yml
osps_br_01_04_justification: Workflows take no manual inputs, and the only collaborator-controlled value used, github.actor, is passed through an environment variable: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish.yml
osps_br_02_02_justification: Each release is a versioned Marketplace release and a GitHub release with the same tag, with the .vsix attached: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/releases
osps_br_07_02_justification: How secrets are stored, accessed and rotated: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#secrets
osps_do_03_01_justification: How to check that the Marketplace serves the same file as the GitHub release, by its SHA-256 digest: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases
osps_do_03_02_justification: Releases come from the verified Marketplace publisher phun-ky, published only by the publish workflow in this repository through Trusted Publishing, and VS Code shows the publisher and checks the Marketplace signature: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases
osps_do_04_01_justification: Only the latest release is supported: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
osps_do_05_01_justification: A release stops getting security updates when the next one is published; fixes ship only as a new release: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
osps_gv_04_01_justification: Collaborators are reviewed, including two-factor authentication, before getting escalated permissions: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#becoming-a-maintainer
osps_qa_02_02_justification: The .vsix contains no compiled software and no dependencies, only the two theme files, the manifest, README, CHANGELOG and LICENSE, so an SBOM would have nothing to list.
osps_qa_04_02_justification: The project has a single repository, so there are no subprojects in other repositories.
osps_qa_06_02_justification: When and how the tests run, locally and in CI: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
osps_qa_06_03_justification: New or changed colours and bug fixes must come with tests: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
osps_qa_07_01_justification: The project has one maintainer, so no non-author approval is possible yet. A review by a maintainer other than the author is required once there is a second maintainer: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#reviews
osps_sa_03_02_justification: Threat model, trust boundaries and attack surface: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md#threat-model
osps_vm_04_02_justification: Vulnerabilities in development dependencies that do not affect the extension are recorded as OpenVEX statements: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/vex.openvex.json
osps_vm_05_01_justification: Thresholds for fixing vulnerability and licence findings in dependencies: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
osps_vm_05_02_justification: Releases are blocked while a shipped dependency has a known high or critical vulnerability (npm audit --omit=dev in the publish workflow); the extension ships none: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
osps_vm_05_03_justification: Dependency review checks every pull request against the GitHub Advisory Database and blocks high or critical findings, as the documented policy says: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml
osps_vm_06_02_justification: The ruleset on main blocks merging while CodeQL reports an error or a high or critical security alert: https://github.com/phun-ky/vscode-accessible-theme/blob/main/SECURITY.md#code-scanning
